, during the last 80,000 years, the vegetation of the Venetial plain was characterized by the following: (i) the presence of Carya and/or Pterocarya in all phases; (ii) the presence of Pinus formations in all phases; and (iii) the presence of temperate taxa only in phases corresponding to climatic warming, in which they were present in variable numbers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the vegetation of the eastern sector of the Veneto coastal plain has undergone significant changes over the past 50,000 years, and that the LGM and the Holocene transgressive phase have left a clear imprint.

, at the eastern end of this sector, the LGM was not as cold as in the rest of the Venetia region; the vegetation was characterized by Pinus, but with significant numbers of other temperate species; the Holocene transgressive phase started around 6840 year BP, and the progradation phase started around 5060 year BP; the Holocene progradation is still in progress.
the eastern sector of the Veneto coastal plain was covered by forested environments until the LGM.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, for the first 50 m of the sedimentary sequence of the eastern Venetia coastal plain, the vegetational and environmental changes observed are in agreement with those known for other sectors of the Venetia plain, and for the rest of Europe.

the eastern end of Venice Lagoon was not a barrier during the last glacial maximum, as has been hypothesized for the western end of the lagoon, and it was probably a lagoon since the early Pleistocene.
, in this sector of the Lagoon, the LGM was a time of low sedimentation, while the Holocene transgressive and regressive phases were characterized by higher rates of sedimentation.
